descriptionChirho: The proper geographical name Goshen, referring primarily to the fertile Egyptian delta region where the Israelites settled during the sojourn (Gen 45:10, 46:28-29, 47:1-6, 50:8), and secondarily to a district in the southern hill country of Judah (Josh 10:41, 11:16, 15:51). All three clusters are grammatical variants: the primary bare or suffixed form 'Goshen/to Goshen' (eng Goshen, spa Goshen/Goshén, hin गोशेन-के, arb جُوشَنَ/جَاسَانَ, kor 고센, swa Gosheni), with article 'the Goshen' (eng the-Goshen, spa Gosén, hin गोशेन, arb جُوشِنَ, kor 그-고센의, swa ha-Gosheni), and with conjunction 'and Goshen' (eng and-Goshen, spa y-Gosén, hin और-गोशेन, arb وَجوشَنُ, kor 그리고-고센, swa na-Gosheni). The Arabic dual attestation جُوشَنَ/جَاسَانَ reflects two transliteration traditions of the same toponym.
